e: After 30 days, access patterns are inconsistent, so S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves each object automatically to the cheapest suitable tier while staying highly available (multi-AZ). A lifecycle rule to clean up incomplete multipart uploads stops paying for abandoned parts. One Zone-IA lacks resiliency, and Standard-IA charges retrieval fees for unpredictable access.

AWS Network Firewall in the path of the private subnet's outbound traffic can use domain list rule groups to allow only approved repository domains and block all other internet traffic. Security groups can't filter by URL or domain, WAF protects inbound web requests, and an ALB doesn't filter outbound traffic.

CloudFront caches static content to offload traffic, and an SQS queue receives the sales requests so they are stored durably and processed by the EC2 workers at their own pace, ensuring that all requests are processed even during sudden spikes. Scaling alone or caching doesn't guarantee that no request is lost.

Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities, and Systems Manager Patch Manager patches instances on a schedule and reports patch compliance for each instance. Macie, GuardDuty, and Detective don't scan for vulnerabilities, and cron jobs or Session Manager aren't patch management.

RDS encryption at rest is enabled when creating the DB instance and uses an AWS KMS key. SSL/TLS certificates from ACM or IAM encrypt data in transit, not at rest, and Secrets Manager stores secrets, not RDS encryption keys.

At 15 Mbps with a 70% cap (about 10.5 Mbps), 20 TB would take far longer than 30 days over the network, so a physical device is needed: AWS Snowball. DataSync, VPN, and Transfer Acceleration are all limited by the bandwidth.

FSx for Windows File Server is a managed Windows file system that integrates with the on-premises Active Directory for authorization, and AWS Client VPN gives remote employees secure access to download files. Public-subnet EC2, signed URLs, or a public endpoint are weaker for confidential files.

The load spike is predictable (the first of every month at midnight), so a scheduled scaling policy can add capacity ahead of time. Reactive CPU-based scaling reacts too slowly to an immediate peak, and CloudFront or ElastiCache don't remove batch calculation load.

AWS Transfer Family offers a managed SFTP endpoint backed by S3 that supports Active Directory authentication, so the customer's SFTP client keeps working unchanged with low operational overhead. DMS, DataSync, or a Windows EC2 SFTP server don't meet the requirements as simply.

EBS fast snapshot restore makes volumes created from the snapshot fully initialized immediately, so instances launched from an AMI built from that snapshot don't suffer first-access latency, which minimizes initialization time when scaling out. The other options don't remove the lazy-loading latency.

Secrets Manager stores credentials encrypted with KMS, integrates with Aurora, and supports automatic rotation with a custom rotation period such as 14 days, with the least effort. Parameter Store lacks native rotation, and file-based approaches need custom rotation code.

Aurora MySQL replicas share the same storage volume as the primary, so replica lag is typically milliseconds, Aurora Auto Scaling adds replicas as load grows, and MySQL-compatible stored procedures need little change. Caching, EC2-hosted MySQL, or DynamoDB require larger changes or more operations.

An Aurora global database replicates data to the secondary Region at the storage layer with low lag. Removing the DB instance from the secondary cluster (a headless cluster) keeps the replicated storage while avoiding instance costs, which is the cheapest DR option; an instance can be added when failing over. DMS or binlog replication cost more and are more complex.

Secrets Manager stores the credentials and has built-in rotation for RDS MySQL (managed rotation schedule), so the application only needs to load credentials from Secrets Manager, with minimal code change. Writing your own rotation Lambda, using KMS directly, or using Parameter Store (no rotation) adds effort.

AWS WAF in front of the ALB with managed or custom rules (such as the SQL injection rule set) blocks SQL injection attempts. Shield Advanced is for DDoS, Inspector scans but doesn't block, and an ALB listener rule can't detect injections.

A Lake Formation blueprint ingests the Aurora data into the data lake, Lake Formation enforces column-level permissions for the marketing team, and Athena (which honors Lake Formation permissions) acts as the QuickSight data source. IAM or S3 bucket policies can't enforce column-level access.

Predictive scaling uses forecasts of historical load to launch instances ahead of time, pre-launching 30 minutes before the jobs, with no capacity analysis by engineers. Scheduled scaling needs the engineers to determine the capacity, and dynamic scaling reacts after the load arrives.

An Aurora global database provides managed cross-Region replication with low lag and fast failover to the DR Region, with the least operational overhead. Self-managed EC2 replication, in-Region Multi-AZ, or restoring backups cost more effort or have longer recovery.

The Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java stores large payloads (up to 2 GB) in S3 and sends a reference through SQS, so messages up to 50 MB work with minimal code changes. SQS's 256 KB limit can't be raised, and EventBridge or EFS would require redesign.

Cognito handles authentication for a small and growing user base, Lambda@Edge runs authorization at CloudFront edge locations for the lowest latency, and CloudFront serves the web application globally, all serverless and cost-effective. Directory Service is costly for fewer than 100 users, and ALB, Beanstalk, or Transfer Acceleration don't serve content globally the same way.

An S3 File Gateway exposes S3 as SMB and NFS file shares to client workstations, keeping the same look and feel, and S3 Lifecycle policies can tier inactive data. FSx File Gateway is for FSx for Windows (SMB only), volume gateway provides block storage, and tape gateway is for backup software.

A Compute Savings Plan gives savings over a 3-year term and lets you change instance family, size, Region, and OS, matching the need to change instance families within 6 months. EC2 Instance Savings Plans and Standard Reserved Instances lock you into a family (and Region), and zonal RIs are even less flexible.

For constant, predictable workloads, provisioned capacity with reserved capacity gives the lowest cost and keeps spending within the forecasted budget, and the Standard-IA table class reduces storage cost for infrequently accessed data. On-demand mode costs more for steady traffic and has no RCU/WCU settings.

To share an encrypted Aurora snapshot with another account, the customer managed KMS key must be shared with that account (add the account to the key policy), and then the snapshot is shared. Default AWS managed keys can't be shared, and unencrypting or downloading snapshots isn't secure or possible.

Multi-AZ gives high availability with automatic failover, and a read replica in another AZ lets the reports run against the replica so transactions on the primary aren't slowed. Restoring snapshots, RDS Custom, or RDS Proxy limits don't address reporting load.
